anchors.title: Transport and social exclusion: Where are we now?

synthesis.paragraph: Seven papers carry the tag "Urban Transport and Accessibility", addressing topics such as learning urban access costs, perceived accessibility of public transport, pandemic responses of transport-disadvantaged young adults, travel behavior beyond high-accessibility neighborhoods, sustainable travel in Swedish youth sports, driver risk-taking in Phnom Penh, and active versus car commuting in short trips. Four papers are grouped under "Older Adults Driving Studies", which covers perceived accessibility of public transport, the origins of the U.S. transportation research workforce, motorcycle conflict severity at roundabouts, and commuting choices for short trips. The tag "Traffic and Road Safety" is shared by four papers, focusing on pandemic transport responses, driver risk-taking in Phnom Penh, workplace road safety culture, and motorcycle conflict severity at roundabouts. Three papers carry the tag "Transportation Planning and Optimization", covering urban access costs, perceived accessibility of public transport, and travel behavior beyond high-accessibility neighborhoods. Outside these groups, one paper evaluates nineteen graph neural network layer types for autonomous vehicle trajectory prediction, another analyzes Tehran's urban diplomacy governance model using a survey of ninety municipal officials, and a third uses smartcard data from Perth to analyze transit hub patronage.
